assessment: The deck converts: four checker-passed stacks each take a four-opponent pod from 40 to 0, and three of them are unbounded. What it cannot do is touch a permanent it does not like. deck-audit measures interaction-breadth at 2 classes of 5 with artifact, graveyard and land flagged; reading the cards narrows that to artifact and land genuinely uncovered, because Bojuka Bog exiles a graveyard and is filed land:tapped. So six of the ten answer named holes in the interaction suite or the protection axis, and four widen an engine component the audit prices at one card. The bench is four cards, so three of them make the list on merit and seven pool picks fill the rest; Sheoldred, Whispering One is the only bench card left in the box. Read the natural_cuts as ten separate one-for-one proposals, not a swap plan — two of them draw from the same any_of group and should not both be spent.

ten.why: A turn-3 Grafdigger's Cage across the table blanks the Gravecrawler recast that stacks 009 and 011 (both pass) are built on, blanks Reassembling Skeleton, Animate Dead, Persist and Victimize with it, and the 79-card maindeck destroys or exiles no artifact at any price — Gate to Phyrexia answers the Cage on your next upkeep and on every upkeep after that.
ten.unlocks: The artifact class, repeatably and for two mana: Cursed Totem, Torpor Orb, an opposing Altar or a Cage all die to a creature you were going to sacrifice anyway, and card_roles files it sac-outlet as well as removal:spot, so the cost is a death trigger for Bastion of Remembrance.

ten.why: Lightning Greaves, Sedgemoor Witch and Yahenni all protect a creature, and the drain that loops in stacks 009, 010 and 011 (all pass) is Bastion of Remembrance, an enchantment none of them can save; Imp's Mischief points the Disenchant somewhere else for {1}{B} at instant speed and pays only that spell's mana value in life.
ten.when: Sleeve it against any pod that holds targeted noncreature removal, and against blue — it also answers the counterspell aimed at your Beseech the Mirror, which is the other way this deck loses a game it had won.

Infinite card draw and near-infinite lifeloss

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Gravecrawler
ten.why: The diagnosis looks for a body that returns for {B} with no other gate, finds none, and is right — but deck-audit lists Pawn of Ulamog among the closers for KILL B (assembled 0.005 unassisted, 0.123 assisted), and the reason is that it replaces the SHAPE rather than the card: a 0/1 Spawn on every nontoken death is the mana half of a loop that never casts anything from a graveyard.
ten.unlocks: Seven recorded lines, and the cheapest of them names only cards already in the 99 — Reassembling Skeleton plus Phyrexian Altar plus this. Nothing here is verified; a resolve-stack run is what would settle whether the Spawn's {C} plus the Altar's {B} really pays the Skeleton's {1}{B} every turn.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite lifeloss, lifegain, death and sacrifice triggers

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Bastion of Remembrance
ten.why: Bastion is the drain in three of the four checker-passed kills and deck-audit prices that component at 0.167 assembled; Bontu's Monument is an each-opponent drain on a noncreature body that fires on the CAST, which is the per-iteration event in both Gravecrawler loops rather than a second copy of the death trigger.
ten.unlocks: A drain that a Toxic Deluge cannot answer, plus {1} off every black creature spell across 28 creatures — the corpus's 'effects that tax or drain every opponent at once', bought in the class the deck can least afford to have one of.

ten.why: The corpus is explicit — 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any' — and land is the class this deck answers zero times; Strip Mine buys it for no spell slot, kills the Nykthos or Cabal Coffers that is beating you on turn 5, and taps for {C} every other game.
ten.unlocks: The land class, and a free out against Maze of Ith, Glacial Chasm and an opposing Urborg. With your own Urborg on the battlefield it is itself a Swamp, so it taps for {B} and counts for Cabal Coffers.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: the lifegain-triggered drain — the Exquisite Blood half
ten.why: Stack 012 (pass) kills a four-opponent pod with Exquisite Blood plus one lifegain-triggered drain, and the deck runs three of those drains against exactly one Exquisite Blood — deck-audit measures that half at 0.069 assembled, 0.425 with tutors, mean turn 5.301; 'Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life' is the same sentence on a 5/5 flying deathtouch body.
ten.unlocks: Three recorded lines, one with each of Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric and South Wind Avatar — a one-card component becomes two, which the corpus still prices below the 31% five-copy mark, so say the ceiling out loud. None is verified.

ten.why: Feed the Swarm is the deck's only answer to a noncreature permanent and deck-audit prices that component at one card, 0.173 assembled — Withering Torment kills a resolved Rest in Peace or an opposing Dictate at instant speed for three mana, which McGuinness calls 'essentially the most any player should pay for interaction'.
ten.unlocks: Depth on the class the deck is thinnest in, and a creature answer that is live on your own turn or theirs; every death it causes is a Bastion of Remembrance and Meathook Massacre trigger, both of which the synergy graph shortlists it beside.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Gravecrawler
ten.why: deck-audit lists Drivnod among KILL B's closers, and the arithmetic is why: every death trigger of a permanent you control fires twice, so Bastion of Remembrance's 40 drain events become 20 and Pitiless Plunderer makes two Treasures per body — the recorded loop with Reassembling Skeleton and Carrion Feeder casts nothing from a graveyard.
ten.unlocks: Five recorded lines and a halving of every drain the deck already runs. No natural_cut is offered: this is a five-drop competing with kills that cost three to five, and the slot it wants is not one to spend on a hunch.

ten.why: It closes nothing the diagnosis names — no mana axis on this deck reads short — and it is here because Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth makes all 36 land copies Swamps, so a turn-4 Crypt Ghast doubles the entire mana base and turns Cabal Coffers into the largest single tap in the game.
ten.when: Sleeve it for grindy pods that reach turn eight, where the goldfish has you at 6.228 mean available mana and Gray Merchant, a large Black Sun's Zenith or a Meathook Massacre for X=5 is the payoff. Leave it in the box against decks that kill on turn five.

ten.why: Grave Pact is already sleeved and this is the same each-opponent edict with flash, so it lands at the end of an opponent's turn and the first Viscera Seer activation on your turn is a table-wide sacrifice before anyone untaps.
ten.when: Sleeve it against token swarms and go-wide creature decks, where a second Grave Pact is a lock rather than redundancy. It does nothing against the Rest in Peace and Grafdigger's Cage pod, which is what the artifact and land answers above are for — and it closes no axis the audit calls short.

bench_verdicts.why: Seven mana against a goldfish mean available mana of 5.223 on turn six and 6.228 on turn eight, in a list whose four checker-passed kills cost three to five — and every job it does is already in the 99 cheaper: Animate Dead, Persist and Victimize reanimate, Grave Pact edicts, and the deck has 28 bodies without paying seven for one.

gaps: Not one line on this page is verified. Every combo_lines_opened entry carries 'needs a stack scenario' by design — Pawn of Ulamog's Reassembling Skeleton loop and Bloodthirsty Conqueror's pairing with Marauding Blight-Priest are the two most worth a resolve-stack run, because both claim to widen a component that a checker-passed stack already depends on.

The obsolescence index lists no replacement for any of the four bench cards, and none of these ten obsoletes a card in the 99 — so no strictly-better claim appears anywhere on this page. The index does list Plague Belcher, Hunted Bonebrute and Treacherous Pit-Dweller as strictly better than Geralf's Messenger, which corroborates that cut without being the reason for it.

deck-audit reports the graveyard class uncovered and no pick here answers it. That is deliberate: the axis carries a probe note saying the detection is an oracle-text heuristic, and reading the cards finds Bojuka Bog exiling a graveyard while filed land:tapped. Tormod's Crypt would have been the pick if the class were really empty; adding it would be depth on a covered class ahead of 'Breadth before depth'.

card-advantage reads 5 against a target of 10 and nothing on this list answers it. The audit's probe names Ayara, Black Market Connections, Castle Locthwain, Plumb the Forbidden and Yawgmoth himself as cards the taxonomy filed elsewhere, and stack 010 (pass) records the commander's draw as MANDATORY and capping that loop — this axis is a question, not a hole, and a draw spell bought against it would be a wasted slot.

The natural_cuts are ten independent proposals and two of them collide: Butcher Ghoul and Yahenni, Undying Partisan are both members of KILL D's seven-card non-Human any_of, so taking Butcher Ghoul narrows it to six and any second cut from that group should be re-measured with goldfish before it is sleeved. Yahenni is also one of only three cards the audit counts under protection, which is why no pick here proposes cutting it.

Phyrexian Reclamation appears on no cut line here on purpose. It is the only repeatable graveyard-to-hand route in the 99 — Takenuma discards itself, and Persist, Victimize, Animate Dead, Malakir Rebirth and Agadeem's Awakening all return to the battlefield once each — which makes it the deck's insurance against graveyard exile in exactly the matchup Gate to Phyrexia is ranked first for.

Meteor Golem answers artifact, enchantment and planeswalker on a body that Animate Dead redeploys for {1}{B}, and it is not on this list only because seven mana arrives after turn eight on the goldfish. If the pod is slow enough that Crypt Ghast is right, Meteor Golem is the eleventh card and the ranking above should be re-read.
